scope: BiliSum real-material Phase 1: images plus transcript plus visual notes to game analysis dossier
target_questions: Can this BiliSum material support a comprehensive and accurate gameplay analysis dossier?
What are the core loop, combat resolution, deckbuilding constraints, in-run economy, and growth routes of Anode Heart: Layer Null?
Which structures can transfer into the current unique-core-card card-battle project?
thesis: The supplied materials support a concise but real Phase 1 dossier: Anode Heart: Layer Null is best described as a collection/deckbuilding card battler whose repeated pleasure comes from rebuilding a deck around color/tag synergies, then resolving dense board-state decisions through summon effects, response windows, typed energy, evolution/growth, and combat spillover. Visual evidence strongly supports the combat and system-surface claims, while market, narrative, and exact long-term progression claims remain under-evidenced.

modules.title: Game Positioning, Basic Facts, And Market Context
modules.claim: The material supports basic positioning as a card-collection and deckbuilding battle game, but not a commercial or market dossier. Facts such as release, sales, audience size, retention, and live-version status are outside the supplied evidence.
open_questions: No verified release, platform, pricing, sales, rating, or live update data in the supplied pack.

modules.title: Global Player Experience And Design Goals
modules.claim: The experienced arc is collection -> deck hypothesis -> battle test -> failure diagnosis -> route/color rebuild. The emotional driver is not only winning one battle, but discovering that a color/tag route changes what counts as a playable hand and a strong board.
open_questions: The pack does not prove how representative this play route is across the full game.

modules.title: Core Gameplay Loop
modules.claim: The core loop is to collect/build a deck, enter regional BO3-style battles, inspect and play cards onto a lane board, resolve summon/status/response/combat effects, then use the result to revise deck composition and route strategy.
open_questions: Exact turn-order and BO3 details should be verified from original footage if this becomes a polished dossier.

modules.title: Full System Architecture Breakdown
modules.claim: The architecture combines collection/regions, deckbuilding constraints, a lane-like unit board, typed energy, card tags, summon/trigger effects, counter/response windows, block/spillover combat, shop/shard economy, and evolution/growth. The strongest system insight is that many layers meet on the combat screen rather than living in separate menus.
open_questions: Exact formulas, maximum board size, full card taxonomy, and route acquisition rules need source verification beyond this pack.

modules.title: Content And Level Structure
modules.claim: Evidence points to color/attribute routes, regional acquisition, bosses, and a transition from colorless to grass/native cards. The pack supports content structure at the route-and-card-family level, not a full content map.
open_questions: The number of regions, boss order, unlock rules, and complete card list are not independently verified here.

modules.title: Numerical Systems And Economy Loops
modules.claim: The visible economy has at least three layers: combat stats HP/BP, typed energy/costs, and a shop/shard-like in-run resource. These layers create hand playability risk and reward routes that generate extra energy, draw, growth, or recovery.
open_questions: Exact shard income, card cost formulas, draw rates, and upgrade math are not fully confirmed.

modules.title: Narrative, Character/IP, Audio-Visual Packaging
modules.claim: Materials are thin for narrative and audio. Visual evidence supports a compact pixel-art UI with creature cards and readable tactical panels, but not a robust story/IP analysis.
open_questions: No direct audio, story, character progression, or worldbuilding evidence was audited.

modules.title: Strengths, Weaknesses, And Transferable Optimizations
modules.claim: The strongest transferable lesson is the way visible card tags, typed costs, response windows, and board feedback let a complex deckbuilding game remain diagnosable. The main risk is cognitive load and draw/energy variance, especially when a deck route lacks enough playable units or matching energy.
open_questions: Need original play sessions or player data to separate one-off variance from systemic friction.
